top_strength: Erik handled a skeptical, budget-conscious customer with real confidence and won the verbal booking. When Richard pushed back on hourly billing — "this is not one of these with these guys are gonna take their time doing this just because it's an hourly rate" — Erik answered head-on with "Absolutely not. No sir" and then backed it with substance: "it's likely that we'd beat this estimate. We regularly do beat our estimates. I just I'm a fan of airing on the side of caution." He also steered the customer to the cheaper Thursday rate unprompted after Richard said he wasn't "looking to spend a ton of money," covered inclusions thoroughly ("the guys we send you the truck, they're driving the fuel that's pushing us down the road. This covers the taxes for your move as well as the insurance for your move"), and used the customer's name throughout. Richard closed the call with "Eric, awesome. Thanks for your help."
coaching_note: The three differentiators that separate Einstein from the cheapest quote never came out of Erik's mouth on a call where the customer was explicitly price-shopping — No Worries Damage Coverage, Meet Your Mover, and the On-Time Guarantee are all zero here. He said only "the insurance for your move," which tells a customer nothing. Richard even handed him the opening: "I don't want things wraps and broken." That is the exact moment to say up to $2,000 to repair, replace, or reimburse accidental damages. The second miss compounds it: the entire Save Your Ass prep speech was skipped on a move where prep was already the customer's own instinct — Richard volunteered "I'll throw it in the car" twice and Erik just said "Not an issue at all" instead of turning it into the consolidation/carload coaching that shortens the move and lowers the bill. Lead with the three differentiators before quoting the rate, then run the prep speech before the close.
phone_presence_notes: Consistently warm and personable — used "Mister Richard"/"Richard" throughout, absorbed the customer's cost skepticism without getting defensive, and the customer ended the call thanking him by name.
